meta.title: Ch 2: Risk Management — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 2 (Risk Management).

questions.q: Which risk can be eliminated through diversification?
questions.why: Beta (systematic) cannot be diversified; idiosyncratic risk averages away in large portfolios.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the diversification boundary is the most-tested risk concept Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Diversification shaves the hills you own, never the mountain the economy builds.

questions.q: A 5% one-day VaR of Rs 2 crore on a portfolio means:
o: On 5 of every 100 days (approx), the one-day loss EXCEEDS Rs 2 crore
5% of portfolio lost in a crash
questions.why: VaR = threshold loss at the confidence level (1−α) over the horizon; tail beyond is unspecified — the 'possible exceedance days' phrasing is the correct reading.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the probability-reading of VaR is the definition test AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: VaR names the line you cross on bad days; it never promises you won't cross it deeply.

questions.q: The key economic difference between hedging and speculation is:
o: Hedging reduces existing exposure; speculation creates exposure for profit
questions.why: Hedge = offset an exposure you already have; speculation = take an open position expecting to profit.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the economic-intent distinction Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Hedging buys certainty for a risk you have; speculation rents a risk you didn't.

questions.q: Scaling daily VaR to 10 days (i.i.d. returns) multiplies it by:
questions.why: Square-root-of-time rule with uncorrelated normal returns: 10-day ≈ daily × √10 — NOT ×10.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the √t rule with its ×t distractor Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Risk stacks like a random walk: by the square root of time, not the clock.

questions.q: A long futures position with initial margin and a large loss below maintenance margin triggers:
o: A margin CALL to top up to INITIAL margin levels (variation margin is separate)
questions.why: Maintenance breach ⇒ variation/margin call bringing account to the maintenance (Indian practice: to initial per exchange norms for many segments) — the exam expects: amount brought to cover shortfall, with contract continuing; do not confuse daily variation margin with maintenance calls.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the margin hierarchy sequence is the plumbing question AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Daily settle the score; when the tank runs dry, refill the tank, not the contract.

questions.q: Portfolio Rs 100 crore, daily σ 1.5%, one-tailed z of 2.33 (95%/99%). Parametric VaR for one and ten days:
questions.why: Daily = 100×1.5%×2.33 = 3.50 crore; 10-day by √10 rule ≈ 11.05 crore (i.i.d. assumption).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the √t scaling with the wrong ×10 distractor AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: Portfolio Rs 100 crore, daily σ 1.5%, one-tailed z of 1.65 (95%/99%). Parametric VaR for one and ten days:
questions.why: Daily = 100×1.5%×1.65 = 2.47 crore; 10-day by √10 rule ≈ 7.83 crore (i.i.d. assumption).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the √t scaling with the wrong ×10 distractor AI prediction, not a certainty.

questions.q: The line between hedging and speculation in a derivatives policy is drawn by:
o: Whether an offsetting exposure exists that the position is sized and aimed to reduce
questions.why: A hedge answers an existing exposure (same notional logic, opposite direction, matched tenor); without an underlying exposure, the same contract is a directional bet — policy documents must define eligible exposures and prohibit naked positions.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — exposure first, instrument second AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: A hedge is an umbrella; speculation is a bet on rain.

questions.q: Hedging jet fuel with crude futures is a cross-hedge; effectiveness then depends mainly on:
o: The stability of the correlation and regression beta (minimum-variance hedge ratio) between jet fuel and crude
questions.why: Cross-hedges replace the untradeable exposure with a correlated proxy; optimal size = 1.0 adjusted by the hedge ratio from regression of spot changes on futures changes — basis-correlation instability is the killer risk.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — same-good hedge: ratio near 1; cross-good: the ratio is the risk AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Borrowed umbrella only works while two weathers agree.

questions.q: A bank reports 1-day 99% VaR of ₹50 crore. Correct interpretation:
o: On 99 of 100 days the loss will not exceed 50 crore (1-day horizon, current positions, normal markets)
50 crore is the worst possible loss
questions.why: VaR = the loss threshold exceeded on (1−c) fraction of days under the model's assumptions; it says nothing about the size of the tail it doesn't measure — hence stress tests and expected shortfall supplement it.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — VaR names the cliff edge, not the depth of the fall Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: 99 days of weather, 1 day of free-fall — and VaR won't tell you how far.

questions.q: Long position hedged with futures; at closing the spot has risen MORE than the futures price. The hedge:
o: Leaves a net gain because the basis (spot − futures) strengthened
questions.why: Perfect hedging requires the spot and futures to move one-for-one; a strengthening basis favours the long spot/short futures hedger (selling the relatively weaker futures) — basis risk is the residue hedging cannot remove.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — hedging converts price risk into basis risk Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Umbrella in one hand, rain in the other — basis is the gap.
